formats.key: Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: Once submitted, sets the owner's krfUSDC vault-share allowance for `spender` to exactly `value`, replacing the old allowance (OZ ERC20PermitUpgradeable.permit -> _approve).
If `value` is type(uint256).max, the allowance is never reduced when spent (ERC20Upgradeable._spendAllowance), so it is unlimited.
The spender can then move up to `value` shares with transferFrom, or redeem/withdraw them for USDC to any receiver (ERC4626 redeem/withdraw spend the same allowance).
Uses up the owner's permit nonce `nonce`. The signature can only be submitted until `deadline`; the allowance it sets does not expire.
formats.shown: Authorize share spending: approve {value} krfUSDC (or 'Unlimited') for {spender} until {deadline}, with share owner, spender, amount, signature deadline and nonce all shown.

findings.title: Permit interpolated intent says 'until {deadline}', which suggests the allowance expires; only the signature does.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json interpolatedIntent "Approve {value} for {spender} until {deadline}"; screen case 3: "Approve Unlimited krfUSDC for 0xEAFC… until 2030-01-01 00:00:00Z". ERC20PermitUpgradeable.permit only checks `block.timestamp > deadline` before _approve; ERC20Upgradeable._approve stores `_allowances[owner][spender] = value` with no expiry.
findings.fix: Use e.g. "Approve {spender} to spend {value} (signature valid until {deadline})", or drop the deadline from the intent.
